About

Security explained simply — so everyone can act on it

I'm Arbaz Ahmed Naveed from Pakistan, building my career as a cybersecurity analyst and ethical hacker. My path is structured and verifiable: Cisco Networking Academy foundations first, then hands-on labs — SQL injection, Burp Suite, web application security — always on my own systems or authorised training labs.

Try it yourself

Scam Spotter — can you tell?

Four real-world situations from my videos. Decide each one, and learn the check that gives the scam away.

Scenario 01

The "bank" text message

"Dear customer, your account will be suspended today. Verify now: bank-secure-verify.xyz — enter your card details and the OTP we send you."

Scam. Banks never ask for OTPs or card details through a link, and real bank messages don't come with strange domains like bank-secure-verify.xyz. Open your banking app directly — never through a message link.

Scenario 02

The courier call

A caller says your parcel is stuck and asks you to read out the 6-digit code just sent to your WhatsApp so they can "release the delivery."

Scam. That code is your WhatsApp verification code — sharing it hands your account to the caller. No courier ever needs it. This is exactly the fake parcel scam from my documentary.

Scenario 03

Turning on 2FA

You open WhatsApp's official settings yourself and switch on two-step verification with your own PIN.

Safe — and smart. Changing security settings inside the official app, on your own initiative, is one of the strongest habits there is. It's how the parcel scam above gets stopped.

Scenario 04

The "easy money" task

A stranger on Telegram offers daily income for liking videos — but first you must deposit a small "activation fee" to unlock bigger tasks.

Scam. Real work pays you — it never asks you to pay first. Task scams start small, show fake earnings, then disappear with the bigger deposit.

Score: 0 / 4 answered

Golden rules

Six rules that stop most scams

  • 01
    Never share an OTP or codeNot with a bank, courier, police officer or "official" — no genuine service ever asks.
  • 02
    Check the link before you tapRead the real domain carefully. One wrong letter means a fake site.
  • 03
    Turn on two-factor authenticationOn WhatsApp, email and banking apps — it blocks account theft even if a code leaks.
  • 04
    Slow down when it feels urgent"Act now or lose everything" is the scammer's favourite pressure trick. Real deadlines allow verification.
  • 05
    Verify on a second channelCall the person or company on a number you already trust — never the number in the suspicious message.
  • 06
    Teach one person todayShare these rules with family. Scammers target the least-informed person in every home.
